financials_multi_year.source: Saudi Aramco Q3 & 9M 2026 Unaudited Financial Results (Nov-26), read 25-Nov-26

observations.notes: 9M26 rev SAR 1,515.88bn ($404.23bn, +20.8% YoY), NI SAR 379.02bn ($101.07bn, +36% YoY), adj NI $98.38bn, capex $35.78bn, gearing 5.5% (down from 6.2% Jun-26). Q326 CFO $38.7bn, Q3 FCF $28.2bn.

debt_maturities.source: Reported 2025/2026 USD bond & sukuk benchmark tranches (excluding legacy 2019/2020/2024 GMTN tranches & lease/project debt).

verdict.stance: Neutral / Sovereign-Anchored Ultra-Low-Cost Energy Giant (Aa3 / A+)
verdict.summary: 9M26 revenue jumped 20.8% YoY to $404.2bn and reported NI rose 36% to $101.1bn (Q3 FCF $28.2bn, downstream EBIT +234% YoY) on stronger refining margins and affiliate gains, pulling gearing down to 5.5%. Sovereign dividend commitments ($21.9bn Q3 base dividend) and Vision 2030 strategic outlays (e.g. $2.6bn HUMAIN AI stake) plus Strait of Hormuz export routing risks anchor credit spreads near the Saudi sovereign.

positives: World's lowest-cost upstream oil & gas reserve base generating $85.4bn FY25 FCF and $28.2bn in Q326 alone.
Minimal balance sheet leverage with 5.5% gearing at 30-Sep-26 (down from 6.2% at Jun-26).
East-West Pipeline provides partial export redundancy around Strait of Hormuz transit bottlenecks.
negatives: Sovereign fiscal and dividend extraction ($21.9bn/qtr base dividend) absorbs bulk of organic FCF.
Heavy multi-year capex ($52.2bn FY25, $35.78bn 9M26) plus non-core strategic tech investments (HUMAIN 49% stake).
Regional conflict & Red Sea / Strait of Hormuz shipping disruption sensitivity.

background.business_overview: World's largest integrated oil, gas, and downstream company; national oil champion of Saudi Arabia.
background.asset_perimeter: Ghawar, Safaniya, Khurais upstream fields, Zuluf increment, Jafurah unconventional gas, Fadhili expansion, global refining/petchems (SABIC 70%).
background.ownership_governance: Majority owned by State of Saudi Arabia (81.48%) and PIF/Sanabil (16%); Tadawul listed (2222.SE).

recent_drivers: Nov-26 (Q3/9M26): Rev $140.5bn in Q3 ($404.2bn 9M), Q3 adj NI $31.2bn (+9.1%), Q3 FCF $28.2bn, gearing 5.5%.
Early 2026: Priced $4.0bn multi-tranche USD bonds (3Y 4.00% to 30Y 6.00%) following $3.0bn 2025 bond/sukuk issues.

catalysts.event: FY2026 Audited Results & FY27 Capex Guidance
catalysts.impact: Tests gearing trajectory, Jafurah ramp, and dividend payout.
Cash outflow check vs Q4 oil & refining margins.

management_guidance_tracker.variance_analysis: Strong Q3 FCF ($28.2bn) compressed gearing sequentially despite $21.9bn dividend.

management_guidance_tracker.management_target: Sustaining + Jafurah/Zuluf growth capex (~$50-55bn FY pace)
management_guidance_tracker.variance_analysis: Q3 capex moderated 16% YoY ($10.52bn vs $12.55bn) while Zuluf crude increment started.

management_questions.question: Quantify East-West Pipeline utilization and incremental export freight/insurance costs during 2026 regional disruptions.
management_questions.relevance: Hormuz disruption resilience underpins sovereign-tight spreads.

management_questions.question: Outline 2027 capital expenditure and non-core AI/mineral JV funding budgets.
management_questions.relevance: Determines whether FCF covers base dividends without incremental debt.

annotations.note: 9M26 rev $404.23bn (+20.8%), NI $101.07bn (+36%), Q3 FCF $28.2bn, gearing improved to 5.5% from 6.2% in Q2.

recovery_analysis.thesis: Ultra-low lifting cost and single-digit gearing provide near-sovereign asset coverage.
